{"self_assessment": "Impact: I laid the bottom line of the fish, the long lower outline running from the nose out to the tail. It's about 37 dominoes and a large share of the body shape, and it ran continuously into the lower tail lobe. The whole picture was connected to the start, with all 115 standing dominoes in the fall by my last check, and it reads as a fish.

Execution: I took my stroke from the shared sketch and laid it as soon as the top line reached the nose, so the lower body went up with no idle time. Once it was down I inspected the line and the joins three times to confirm nothing was broken, then kept my hands off so we wouldn't cause a bump. I didn't need to fix anything.

Collaboration: I backed the plan Maya proposed and the split of strokes, and asked Priya to sketch it so we had one shared drawing to build from. I kept the table informed on progress, told Leo when the line was reaching his lobe so he could pick it up, and stayed out of everyone's way during the final stretch.

Leadership: I helped get the table moving quickly by proposing a clear assignment of strokes: top line, bottom line, and one tail lobe each. That let all four of us work in parallel from early on. I also set the handoff order between my line and Leo's lobe, and I steered us to stop touching the build once it was connected so it would fall cleanly.", "my_share_percent": 30}
